question: A platform team wants to prevent Claude Code from ever running rm -rf against production paths, regardless of what the model decides to do. Which hook event should they use to guarantee the command never executes?
options: A) PostToolUse, because it fires after the command runs and can roll back the result
B) PreToolUse, because it fires before the tool call executes and can deny it
C) Notification, because it fires when Claude Code sends a status message about the command
D) Stop, because it fires when Claude finishes responding and can flag the transcript
correct_answers: B) PreToolUse, because it fires before the tool call executes and can deny it
explanations: Incorrect. PostToolUse fires after the tool has already succeeded, so by the time it runs the destructive command has already executed.
Correct. PreToolUse fires before the tool call runs and supports permissionDecision: deny, which stops the command from ever executing.
Incorrect. Notification only reports status events like permission prompts or idle states; it has no ability to block tool execution.
Incorrect. Stop fires once per turn when Claude finishes responding, long after any tool calls in that turn have already run.
